description_full: Titan America SA, through its subsidiaries, manufactures and supplies heavy building materials and services in the United States. The company offers cement and cementitious materials, ready-mix concrete, aggregates, concrete blocks, fly ash, and other ancillary products. It also engages in trading, real estate holdings, insurance brokerage, and transportation brokerage activities. The company was founded in 1989 and is based in Brussels, Belgium. Titan America SA operates as a subsidiary of Titan Cement International S.A.
ceo_bio: Mr. Vassilios S. Zarkalis | President, CEO & Director | Age 64
culture_narrative: Employs approximately 2K people. Revenue per employee of $652K ranks in the above the sector median among Basic Materials peers. Each employee generates $53K of free cash flow annually.
financial_summary: Titan America SA is a mid-cap basic materials business with a $2.1B market cap on $1.7B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +2% over the past three years, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.
Returns on capital run at 17% against a 9% cost of capital, a 9-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it, with gross margins sitting at 26%.

The business throws off $135M in free cash flow — roughly 8 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.59× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.5× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 11.9×.

Net dilution runs at 5.5% annually, transferring value from owners to stock-based comp, and insiders hold 87% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.

sector_headwinds.text: Elevated short interest (12.4% of float) — sophisticated money is betting the other way
Weakness in commodity prices pressures materials companies
Commodity price volatility and cost-curve position — in a downturn only the lowest-cost producer has a business, and the rest carry the overhead.
Environmental remediation liability — tightening regulations on emissions, tailings, and water use create open-ended balance-sheet risk that grows with each legislative cycle.
Trade policy and tariff whiplash — materials producers are first-order casualties of protectionist swings, and margin gets squeezed from both input and output pricing.

sector_tailwinds: Reinvestment rate supports 17% organic growth capacity — capital is compounding inside the business
Shares offer a 17% margin of safety against estimated fair value
Trading near the bottom of its 52-week range — the market is offering a discount
Returns on capital have been remarkably steady for 5 years — durability is the real test of a moat
Piotroski score 7/9 — financials improving across profitability, leverage and efficiency
Healthy payout ratio leaves room for both dividend growth and reinvestment

sect: Its 16% operating margin runs 7pp above the Basic Materials median (9%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.

The price sits near the bottom of its 52-week range, 43% below the high.

val: The stock trades 17% below its DCF fair value of $13.58, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 22%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $10.90 to $17.16 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Basic Materials peers: P/FCF 15.4 vs 22.4 (sector median).
Earnings yields are attractive: an FCF yield of 6.5% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 10.3% (vs the 8% bar).

The price implies 1.2% annual cash-flow growth, 3pp less than the model expects.
prof: ROIC of 17% clears the cost of capital of 8.7% by 9pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have been steady (CV 0.02).
It runs a 26% gross margin and converts 8% of revenue into free cash flow.

growth: Revenue has compounded at 1.8% over 3 years.

own: Insiders own 86.7%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 16%.
Insiders have only bought over the past year (1 purchase, net $299K bought).
Net share issuance leaves shareholder yield negative (-5.5%), diluting holders.
Short interest is elevated at 12.4% of the float, 13.4 days to cover.
people: With about 2,554 employees, each generates about $652K of revenue, in line with the Basic Materials median.
